assessed_not_shipped.evidence: Audited the suite (~28 candidate `assert x == CONST`). They split into (a) LOCAL test constants — PAL/PARA/MIXED/WIDTH/BASE/TIP_KEYS, all defined in the test file (a bare-name rule false-positives on every one), and (b) CUT-imported constants — C.TIP_ID/NESTED_ID, FREQ_BAND_TOP_X, _LINK_EXTERNAL/_NAMED — which are LEGITIMATE semantic-category assertions (which overlay slot / which freq band / which link color), NOT tautologies. Flagging (b) is the DSpot trap (mutation-killing != developer-valued): it penalises GOOD symbolic-constant practice. ast-grep is syntactic — it can neither distinguish good-(b) from a true change-detector nor correlate the import that would even identify (b).
assessed_not_shipped.decision: NOT shipped as a lint. The genuine 'expected value derived to match output' case is already covered PRECISELY by the DYNAMIC Objective-gate anti-cheat in tools/heal_gate.py (_cut_derived), which knows the specific CUT module + the specific edit. Per the SPEC's no-instrument-on-plausibility + keep-noisy-detectors-out-of-the-gate discipline (cf. Assertion-Roulette/Eager-Test), a static version is net-negative on this suite.
